unique_world.visual_theme: A dry valley with reeds, ferns, bird pools, dark damp patches and white salt crusts in three parts of the valley

primary_mechanic.text: In three rounds, read the signs the board names (reeds, damp dark soil, birds coming to drink, ferns, no white salt crust) and dig only where every sign is present. A dry hole names the sign that was missing. Each spring found opens a reading: the spring given to Ayyub (peace be upon him) (38:41-44) and the call to judge with truth (38:26). The springs are a learning game, not a retelling of the event.

secondary_activities: a blessed Book to think about (38:29)
unique_world.narrative_structure: The sign, three rounds of reading the land, then the closing reading
world_assets: reeds, ferns, damp soil, birds and salt crusts at several spots
dig spots that become small pools
environment_behaviour: a correct dig fills with water
a wrong dig leaves a dry hole
unique_world.learning_objective: Practise careful looking and thinking (38:29) and learn about Ayyub's patience (38:41-44)

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: Wisdom, Responsibility, and Patience
story_library.children_narration: Dawud was given wisdom and responsibility. Sulayman was blessed with a remarkable kingdom. Ayyub faced suffering but remained devoted to Allah. The surah also recalls Adam and the arrogance of Iblis. Together, these accounts teach us to use our blessings wisely and remain humble.

world_idea.title: The Chambers of Wisdom
world_idea.description: Explore different educational environments about justice, responsibility, gratitude, and patience, each based on a separate narrated passage.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: Adam and Iblis (38:71-85) are reading only, as unseen matters.
